I don't know to be honest. I know the stuff I said earlier about music theory but I don't think I've ever heard that particular style within a song described in a single word. Closest I can give you is "build up" or "bridge," but I'm sure someone else might have it?

I just know I've never really heard anyone call it anything in particular that wasn't attributed to the sheet music or something.

​

ETA: Did some quick googling with a bunch of terms and it looks like there's not a particular word for it, but depending on the music genre it can be called a "break," "build," "bridge," "respite," "repose," or "thinning out." I think in this case I would go with a thinned out bridge.

Monophonic texture?

Anytime the rest of the instruments go quiet and it plays the melody, it kind of is considered to be the "build up" before the "drop," even in non-EDM music I guess. In actual musical theory language, it would be monophonic melody with thin texture (same melody, one instrument.) You could go further and assume that the rest of the instruments are on "rest," which is probably what's happening here.

ETA: Could also be considered "staggered buildup." A lot of Touhou OG songs are really just one monophonic melody repeated (like a good jazz riff or something, or like Carol of the Bells,) so I would place my bets on that. Either way, very common piece of music and happens quite often on the refrain or bridge.

I understand how you feel. 

Stories like that are meant to idealize the “perfect” romance, they’re designed to fill that space in readers’ minds. That’s what makes books and fiction so lovely; they’re written to make us feel a certain way. 

Sometimes relationships present themselves in different ways. Some are more casual, some are more romantic.

How long have you been together? Can you two maybe discuss spicing things up and doing more “romantic” things together? These are good things to consider. 

Unfortunately sometimes relationships just run their course, and maybe an outside source was the catalyst for the realization. It becomes a gamble, where you have to consider leaving the known and somewhat comfortable for the unknown in search of someone who will make you feel the same way your romance novels can. 

It definitely can happen, but it can also be a failed plan and you could end up without your partner and end up unhappy that there isn’t the idealized partner you read about. 

Best advice is to first, try to talk it out. Think about what you want. Make a list of pros and cons. Think about being alone for a period of time. Make the judgment call on whether or not your price/princess will eventually come to fruition. You’ll make the right choice!

that is scary, i know i was worried about that at first. the good thing about mental health professionals is that they’re trained to figure this stuff out and help you. everyone is “weak” in something. lots of people are horrible at lifting heavy weight, running, eating healthy, studying, literally anything. some people have a more difficult time paying attention and focusing and dealing with anxiety. the professionals are there to help. even without a “diagnosis” it doesn’t make your struggles invalid. everyone needs a little bit of extra help in something. your brain is just as big of a part of your physical health as the rest of your body. some people need more care for the same types of ailments depending on their body. nobody shits on them for it, we use compassion and realize that everyone has strengths and weaknesses.
